name: Fold clothes efficiently
blurb: Two methods worth knowing: the file fold for drawers, so you can see everything at once, and the ranger roll for packing. Both take one session to learn.
steps: Learn the file fold: fold each item into a small rectangle that stands on its own, then store them vertically so every item is visible.
Learn the ranger roll for travel: tuck the item into its own waistband or hem so the roll cannot come undone.
Learn to fold fitted sheets by tucking each corner into the next — the one folding skill that genuinely defeats most people.
Learn the two-second t-shirt fold as a party trick and a time saver.
Learn what should be hung rather than folded: structured garments, knitwear on shelves not hangers.
Reorganise one drawer entirely with the file method and see whether you actually keep it up.
tips: Stacked clothes mean you wear the top three items forever. Vertical filing is the whole point.
Fold on a flat surface, not on your lap, if you want a consistent shape.
proof: A drawer where every item is visible and stands upright, still tidy a month later.
